text:
maria: quick flagging — customers reported "quota doubling" after we rolled the new routing cookie for v2. looks like some requests are served by v1 even when the client keeps X-Api-Version: v2. console shows sudden drops in v2 affinity. :grimacing:

tom: can you paste a minimal trace? suspect mismatch between edge cookie and central token mapping.

maria: here's a shortened trace from one affected tenant (sanitized):
```
Request A -> Authorization: Bearer T.1  X-Api-Version: v2  => Response: Set-Cookie: __rwd_aff=abc123; Max-Age=30; Path=/
Request B (same client, 40s later) -> Authorization: Bearer T.1  X-Api-Version: v2  => No __rwd_aff cookie in request, served_variant=v1-legacy
```

sara: interesting — which clients are stripping cookies? mobile sdk? the http cli?

maria: narrow sample: two customers use a CDN/proxy that strips cookies on outgoing requests. other customers (web) are fine.

kevin: root cause hypothesis: we introduced ephemeral cookie-based affinity to reduce header bloat, but we didn't backfill a durable mapping in the token->route store. when cookies are missing we should consult the central store keyed by token hash. current edge code falls back to default v1 route. also telemetry attribution uses served_variant as the routing key rather than token-origin, so usage shows up under v1 separately.

tom: so problem is both routing (fallthrough) and metrics (mis-attribution). agree we need two fixes: 1) routing fallback to token->route lookup, 2) metrics change to attribute requests to origin_token_version when present.

ops-bot: deploy: routing-edge:release-2026.03.12 applied to edge-eu-1 at 2026-03-12T02:14Z by @release-ci

sara: suggestion: short-term revert — flip console flag to restore X-Route-Affinity header behavior (drop cookie) for all tenants while we implement a robust fallback. Long-term: keep cookie for perf but ensure central backfill + make telemetry attribute by token_id.

maria: agreed. proposed rollout plan:
- STEP 0 (now): add dashboard panel and alert (affinity-loss-rate)
- STEP 1 (30m): flip console feature-flag to header-affinity fallback for all regions
- STEP 2 (2h): patch edge to consult token->route store when cookie missing
- STEP 3 (24h): revert to cookie flow with central-store backfill + telemetry attribution

kevin: I'll build the dashboard. query draft (Prometheus-ish):
```
sum by (tenant) (rate(requests_total{api_version="v2", served_variant!="v2"}[5m])) / sum by (tenant) (rate(requests_total{api_version="v2"}[5m]))
```
label it affinity_loss_percent. alert if >0.2% for 10m for customers with v2 enabled.

tom: devex note: we should also publish a short SDK advisory — "If you use intermediaries that strip cookies, set preserve_headers=true or pin X-Route-Affinity". but try not to blame customers; set migration guidance.

sara: metric change — we need to add a derived dimension token_origin that peers from Authorization header (hash) and use it in billing attribution pipelines. that's a quick change in metrics ingestion layer (no downstream schema change).

maria: owners + ETA:
- kevin: dashboard + alert (30m)
- infra (tom): flip console flag (30-60m)
- edge team (tom): implement token->route lookup fallback (4h)
- metrics (sara): add token_origin attribution to ingestion (6h)
- devex (maria): publish SDK advisory (1h)

ops-bot: incident-note: affinity-fallback-investigation tagged infra/edge/metrics/devex priority-high.

kevin: putting dashboard up in grafana and wiring PagerDuty for the alert. will also create a small canary set (10 tenants) to test the fallback before global flip.

maria: canary plan: enable header-affinity fallback for 10 tenants (mix of CDN and web) for 1h. watch affinity_loss_percent and per-tenant billing deltas. if stable, promote global.

sara: one more thing — audit logs. add a field in edge logs when fallback happens (reason=cookie_missing -> token_lookup_attempted). that'll help validate fixes post-deploy.

tom: rolling this into a hotfix PR now. will tag for review. aiming to have the flag flip + dashboard in <2h.

maria: thanks all. follow-ups: ping thread when canary is live and when we promote. keeping customers updated via support with a brief "we reverted temporary change and are rolling a fix" message. :thermometer_face:
